subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated GPU scope, scaling buckets & procurement path
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alec Torres <alec.torres@quantix.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated GPU scope, scaling buckets & procurement path

Thanks again for taking time today — appreciate the clear context on Quantix's inference runway. Below is a short recap so we have a shared understanding and a set of next steps.

Quick recap of pain points you shared:
- Latency spikes during nightly re-ranking and live multi-tenant inference (esp. 00:00-04:00 PST).
- Data isolation requirements for PHI-adjacent feature sets (need per-tenant isolation lanes).
- Predictable unit cost for inference to make business-case for product expansion.

Goals we discussed:
- Pilot dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) for core production traffic: initial target 8 x A100-equivalent slots with room to burst to +4 racks.
- Isolation lanes for 2 PHI-sensitive customers, with tenant-level VPC peering and no shared KV cache.
- SLA targets: 99.95% uptime, p95 token latency target 120ms on your 2k token tail workload.

Technical notes from call:
- Your SLO is driven by a mix of short chat requests (<=128 tokens) and heavy rerank jobs that average 1600 tokens. We recommended splitting into light/medium/heavy routing buckets to optimize cost and tail latency.
- We sketched a fallback policy: if dedicated pool saturated, route non-PHI traffic to a cheaper multi-tenant fallback model with automatic prefix cache warming.

Proposed 'scaling buckets' (first pass):
- Light: 0-256 tokens, routed to quantized variant (q4) in shared pool for cost savings.
- Medium: 257-1024 tokens, routed to dedicated pool; soft auto-scale up if utilization >70% for 5m.
- Heavy: >1024 tokens, pinned to isolated racks with pre-warmed KV cache and guaranteed concurrency.

Action items / owners:
- Quantix: share current monthly token volumes by bucket + expected 12mo growth (Alec / Priya) — due Wed 09/30 EOD.
- Redwood: provide a draft SOW and pricing sketch for 8-slot reserved pool + burst lanes (Marissa) — ETA Thu 10/01 COB.
- Both: schedule a technical deep-dive on isolation implementation (Ben to propose times) — aim next week.

Attachments referenced: Quantix M A P_v1.pdf (procurement summary you shared) — I attached a short SLA and latency tradeoff CSV and a sketch of isolation lanes.

If anything above looks off, flag and I’ll update. Otherwise we’ll circulate the SOW draft tomorrow.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sla-latency-table.csv (text/csv)]
[Attachment: isolation-lanes-sketch.png (image/png)]

From: Alec Torres <alec.torres@quantix.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@quantix.ai>, procurement@quantix.ai, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated GPU scope, scaling buckets & procurement path

Thanks Jordan — clean summary, appreciate it. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Volumes: we'll send a CSV with historicals + projected growth, but to set expectations: current monthly tokens ~1.8B, with 35% monthly growth in the last 3 months. Peak windows are very spiky (nightly rerank).

2) Isolation: PHI customers need both logical and network isolation. Logical = separate KV us-east caches and no cross-tenant caching; Network = private peering and distinct subnets. Can Redwood support per-tenant KVM keys for encryption-at-rest?

3) Procurement: procurement@quantix.ai handles contracts — they prefer a single SOW + purchase order flow. We will ask for an enterprise pricing sheet and a Net30 payment term option.

Next steps from our side: Priya will upload the token-by-bucket CSV by EOD tomorrow. Also open to a technical call specifically on key management and cache segregation.

—Alec
Director, Platform Engineering
Quantix AI

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated GPU scope, scaling buckets & procurement path

Alec — quick replies inline and a couple attachments attached to make procurement easier.

- KMS / per-tenant keys: yes, Redwood Private can integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / HSM) and we can scope per-tenant key policies in the SOW. I attached a one-page KMS checklist.
- Isolation lanes: we recommend two physical isolation lanes (PHI lane: dedicated racks with no shared KV; Near-PHI lane: network-isolated but can share cached weights). The isolation-lanes-sketch.png shows the recommended topology.
- SLA & latency: for the reserved 8-slot configuration, rough targets: 99.95% monthly uptime; p95 token latency for medium bucket ~95-120ms depending on model variant; heavy bucket latency will be higher but guaranteed concurrency. See attached CSV for the latency ranges per model variant.

Procurement notes: we can do SOW + PO, and we typically accept Net30 for enterprise customers after credit check. Pricing sketch in SOW will include an item for burst rack-hours and a 20% discount for a 12mo commit.

I've uploaded the draft SOW to the shared Drive link (below) and attached the SLA latencies. Jordan — I'll circulate the SOW by COB today. Ben — can you propose two slots for the deep-dive (Thu/Fri next week)?

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Alec Torres <alec.torres@quantix.ai>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@quantix.ai>, procurement@quantix.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated GPU scope, scaling buckets & procurement path

Thanks Marissa and Jordan — this is exactly the level we need. Priya uploaded the token breakdown to the Drive folder (link below). Procurement will review the SOW once you circulate it; they like to see explicit billing line items for reserved slots, burst hours, and networking/peering.

A couple final asks before SOW finalization: 
- Can Redwood include a short failure-mode appendix that describes behavior when the dedicated pool is fully saturated (routing decisions, throttling, notification/alerting cadence)?
- For the PHI lane, confirm that there will be no shared KV cache and that audit logs for access will be retained for 12 months.

If you can add those two items to the SOW draft, procurement can get an internal review started this week. Otherwise looks good — let's lock a technical deep-dive for Thurs 10/7 (Ben to propose times).

Alec
Director, Platform Engineering
Quantix AI
